blockdesc-buckingmill-frame-*: The frame of a mechanically powered pair of drag saws that cross-cut tree trunks into logs. Fit two saw sashes, a crankshaft, feed levers and two blade kits to assemble it.
error-need-sash: Each blade kit goes into a saw sash. Fit another sash first.
error-blades-fitted: Both blade kits are already fitted.
error-blade-metal: Both blade kits must be the same metal. This mill has {0} blades.
error-not-a-part: That is not a part of this mill.
error-trunk-cut: The trunk is cut too far to take out.
error-no-logging: This mill cannot work with the installed Logging Expanded.
error-incomplete: Assemble the mill before loading a trunk.
error-bed-full: There is already a trunk in the mill.
error-saws-rising: The saws are still rising. Wait until they are back at the top.
info-committed: Too far cut to take the trunk out
info-nopower: Not turning fast enough, connect a turning axle
handbook-assembly-text: Place the frame where the whole machine has room, then fit Immersive Woodworking's sawmill parts with rightmouse, in any order: two saw sashes, a crankshaft, feed levers and two blade kits of the same metal. Each blade kit goes into a sash, so fit a sash before each kit. No carriage is needed. The crankshaft strokes the two saws back and forth across the trunk, and they sink through it under their own weight. When they reach the bottom they trip the levers, which engage a windlass that winds them back up on ropes to a latch at the top. ctrl + rightmouse takes a blade kit back out. The other parts come back only when you break the frame, which drops every fitted part.
handbook-power-text: Connect a turning axle to the power side of the frame. The assembled mill is a heavy load, twice a plank sawmill's, and it only cuts while its shaft turns at a fair speed. Until it is assembled it barely loads the shaft.
handbook-trunks-text: The mill cuts Logging Expanded tree trunks of any size, one at a time. Trunks must have their branches removed first while Logging Expanded asks for that. Load a trunk with rightmouse, holding it, or with an empty hand to take one from your hotbar or backpack. A trunk storage rack standing against the infeed side, on the ground, feeds the running mill: it takes the rack's top trunk about once a second whenever it is empty and its saws are back at the top. A branched trunk on top of the rack holds the line until you deal with it. ctrl + rightmouse takes the trunk back out, but only before a quarter of it is cut.
handbook-yield-text:
Every log stored in a trunk takes 8 turns of the shaft and gives 2 logs of its wood, which drop out of the output side. A cut trunk's resin and branches are lost, as on a sawhorse.

After each cut, and after a trunk is taken back out, the saws wind back up to the top, which takes 6 turns of the shaft from the bottom. The next trunk can only go on once they are up.

Each blade kit loses 1 durability for every 4 logs stored in a cut trunk, rounded up. A worn out kit breaks and the mill stops, its saws where they are, until a new one is fitted. These figures are the defaults of ModConfig/buckingsawmill.json.
